mainTopic: The ברייתא's derivation of the laws of זבה from the פסוקים, the question of פסוקים versus הלכה למשה מסיני, and the closing of מסכת נדה.
overview: A ברייתא works through the פסוק about a זבה (ויקרא 15:25-26), word by word. First it shows which days after her נדה days count as days of זיבה. Some days come from extra words in the פסוק, and days up to the tenth come from a comparison with the fourth day. The eleventh day comes from 'בלא עת נדתה', but the twelfth day is left out because it is not fit for the counting of 'או כי תזוב'. The ברייתא then teaches that bleeding for three, two, or even one day counts. It also teaches that a זבה makes the man who is with her טמא, but a זב does not, even though a קל וחומר seemed to say he should. She also makes משכב ומושב טמא, and after one or two days of bleeding she counts only one clean day. The גמרא asks how these laws can come from פסוקים if they are a הלכה למשה מסיני. It answers that רבי עקיבא learns them from פסוקים, while רבי אלעזר בן עזריה holds they are a הלכה. רבי אבא then proves from 'על נדתה' that bleeding at night also makes her a זבה. The מסכת closes with דבי אליהו's teaching that whoever learns הלכות every day is promised עולם הבא, followed by the הדרן.

steps.title: The verse teaches bleeding right after her נדה days
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא reads the words 'not in the time of her נדה' as meaning bleeding that comes close to, right after, her נדה days.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'not in the time of her menstruation.' This means bleeding that comes close to her menstruation.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא quotes a few words from the פסוק about a זבה. It explains that they refer to bleeding that comes right after her days of נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the bleeding is 'not in the time of her נדה.' So the ברייתא understands that it is talking about the period right after her נדה days end. This is the starting point. Bleeding then can make her a זבה.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman in her regular menstrual period (the seven days of נדה)
A woman who becomes impure through bleeding that comes outside her regular נדה time
Close to her menstruation, right after her נדה days

phrases.english: "Not in the time of her menstruation"
(Beyond her menstruation) means close to her menstruation.
phrases.notes: The words in round brackets are in some versions and not in others.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the ברייתא's reading of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bleeding right after the נדה days falls under the laws of זבה.

steps.title: What about bleeding one day after her נדה days?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know that bleeding one day after her נדה days also counts for זבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So far I only know about bleeding close to her menstruation. Where do we learn about bleeding that is one day away from her menstruation?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא admits that the first words only cover bleeding right after her נדה days. It asks for a source for bleeding one day later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'close to her נדה' sounds limited to the very next day. So the ברייתא looks for a reason to extend the rule one more day. This is a standard 'I only have X, where do we learn Y?' question.

keyTerms.meaning: I only have (so far I can only learn this case)
Separated or distant from
From where do we learn it?

phrases.english: And I have only bleeding close to her menstruation;
from where do we learn bleeding one day separated from her menstruation?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out that step 1 is limited and asks how to extend it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source for treating bleeding one day after the נדה days as זיבה.

steps.title: The extra words 'or if she has a discharge' add one day
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from the next words of the פסוק, 'or if she has a discharge.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Or if she has a discharge.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question from step 2. It points to another phrase in the same פסוק, which adds bleeding that is one day away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'or if she has a discharge beyond her נדה' are an extra phrase in the פסוק. The ברייתא uses them to include one more day beyond 'close to her נדה.'

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (the source is these words)
'Or if she has a discharge', words from the פסוק used to add a case

phrases.english: The verse states: "Or if she has a discharge."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'or if she has a discharge' include bleeding one day after her נדה days.

steps.title: What about two through ten days after?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know the rule also covers bleeding two through ten days after her נדה days.
steps.simpleTranslation: So far I only know about one day. Where do we learn to include bleeding that is two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, or ten days away? Where do we learn it?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes further. The extra phrase only added one day, so now it asks about every day up to ten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase of the פסוק has been used to add only one day. No more words are left to add the rest. So the ברייתא needs a different kind of source. This sets up the comparison in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: To include (to add more cases to the rule)

phrases.english: I have only one day;
from where do we learn to include bleeding separated by two, three,
four, five, six, and seven,
eight, nine, or ten days? From where do we learn it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Points out that step 3 only added one day and asks about the rest.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source for treating bleeding two through ten days after the נדה days as זיבה.

steps.title: Comparing the tenth day to the fourth day
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers with a comparison. The fourth day can count as a single sighting and can complete a set of three days of זיבה. The tenth day can do both, so it is included too.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can say this: we find that the fourth day can count as a single sighting and can also be a day of זיבה. So I will include the tenth day too, since it can also count as a single sighting and also be a day of זיבה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers step 4 with logic instead of extra words from the פסוק. The fourth day is already known to be included, and the tenth day has the same two features, so it is included as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fourth day has two features. If she sees blood once, she counts one clean day for it (ספירה). If it is her third day of bleeding in a row, she becomes a full זבה (זיבה). The tenth day has both of those features too. So the ברייתא says it gets the same law, and the days in between are covered as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as we find (bringing a known case to compare)
Fit for counting: a single sighting for which she counts one clean day
Fit for זיבה: able to be the third day in a row that makes her a full זבה
So too I will bring (include the new case in the same law)

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק directly adds the first two days after נדה. The rest of the days, up to the tenth, are added by comparing them to the fourth day. They share its two features: they can count as a single sighting, and they can complete three days of זיבה.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Fit for counting' here does not mean the seven clean days of a full זבה. It means that one sighting needs one clean day to be counted against it.

phrases.english: You say: just as we find with the fourth day,
that it is fit for counting and fit for זיבה,
so too I will bring the tenth day,
since it is fit for counting and fit for זיבה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 by comparing the tenth day to the fourth day.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The tenth day shares both features of the fourth day, ספירה and זיבה, so it is included in the laws of זבה.

steps.title: What is the source for the eleventh day?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know that bleeding on the eleventh day after her נדה days also counts as זיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know to include the eleventh day?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא has already covered days one through ten. Now it asks about the eleventh day. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 used a comparison to reach the tenth day. That comparison only went as far as day ten, so the eleventh day needs its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: to include, to add a case into the rule
the eleventh day (after her נדה days)

phrases.english: And from where do we know to include the eleventh day?
phrases.notes: He means bleeding on the eleventh day after her seven נדה days are over.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Extends the list of included days from the tenth to the eleventh.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק source that includes the eleventh day as a day of זיבה.

steps.title: The eleventh day comes from 'not in the time of her נדה'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers from the words 'בלא עת נדתה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'Not in the time of her נדה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that the words 'not in the time of her נדה' include the eleventh day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison to the fourth day in step 5 only reached the tenth day. The ברייתא uses the words 'בלא עת נדתה' as one more inclusion, and that brings in the eleventh day. It does not include every day outside נדה; steps 8-11 show the twelfth day is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the פסוק teaches' – the source is in the words of the פסוק
'not in the time of her נדה' – words from ויקרא 15:25

phrases.english: The verse states: 'Not in the time of her menstruation.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words 'בלא עת נדתה' include the eleventh day.

steps.title: Maybe the twelfth day is also included?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the same words might include the twelfth day too.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think I should include even the twelfth day.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks whether the rule should keep going and include day twelve as well. This sets up a quick 'no'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the פסוק includes days outside of נדה, it seems that there is no clear stopping point. So the ברייתא checks whether day twelve fits too.

keyTerms.meaning: 'one might think' – a possible idea that is about to be rejected
the twelfth day

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מְרַבֶּה אַף שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר?
phrases.english: One might have thought that I include even the twelfth day?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל שֶׁאֲנִי מְרַבֶּה אַף שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the limit of the source given in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the inclusion go on to the twelfth day?

steps.title: No, the twelfth day is not included
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers that the twelfth day is not included.
steps.simpleTranslation: You must say: no.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא says no. The days of זיבה stop at eleven.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So the window of זיבה is exactly eleven days. The reason comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: no

phrases.english: You must say: No.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the idea raised in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The twelfth day is not a day of זיבה.

steps.title: Why include eleven but leave out twelve?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what makes the eleventh day different from the twelfth.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see that made you include the eleventh day and leave out the twelfth?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks for the reason behind the line it drew between day eleven and day twelve. This sets up the explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'no' in step 9 was not enough. The ברייתא wants a real difference between the two days, so that the cutoff is not random.

keyTerms.meaning: 'what did you see' – what reason do you have
to leave out, to exclude

phrases.english: And what did you see to include the eleventh day
and to exclude the twelfth day?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the ruling of step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The logic that separates day eleven from day twelve.

steps.title: Eleven fits the counting of 'או כי תזוב', twelve does not
steps.stepSummary: The eleventh day is fit for the counting learned from 'או כי תזוב', and the twelfth day is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: I include the eleventh day because it is fit for the counting of 'or if she has a discharge.' I leave out the twelfth day because it is not fit for the counting of 'or if she has a discharge.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא explains the cutoff. Day eleven can still be part of the זיבה counting, but day twelve cannot.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The test is whether the day can take part in the counting that the words 'או כי תזוב' are about. The eleventh day passes this test, so it is a day of זיבה. The twelfth day does not, so it is outside the window.

keyTerms.meaning: fit, able to count
counting (of days connected to זיבה)
'or if she has a discharge' – words from ויקרא 15:25

steps.whatToRemember: The days of זיבה run for eleven days after נדה. The eleventh day is included and the twelfth is not, because only the eleventh is fit for the counting of 'או כי תזוב'.

phrases.english: I include the eleventh day —
as it is fit for the counting of 'or if she has a discharge,'
and I exclude the twelfth day —
as it is not fit for the counting of 'or if she has a discharge.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Day eleven is fit for the counting of 'או כי תזוב' and day twelve is not.

steps.title: What about bleeding for only two days?
steps.stepSummary: So far the ברייתא has only taught about three days of bleeding. Now it asks how we know that two days also count.
steps.simpleTranslation: I only have a source for three days. From where do we know about two days?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to a new question: does bleeding for fewer than three days also make her טמאה? It begins with two days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier lesson spoke about three days of bleeding. The ברייתא now asks whether a shorter bleeding, of two days, is also covered.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I only have' – the source so far covers only this case
three days of bleeding

phrases.english: And I have derived only three days;
phrases.notes: He means three days in a row of bleeding during the זיבה days.

phrases.english: from where do we know two days?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from which days count to how many days of bleeding count.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that two days of bleeding also make her טמאה.

steps.title: 'Days' includes two days
steps.stepSummary: The word 'ימי' (days) is plural, and that covers two days.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'days.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers from the word 'ימי', which means 'days'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The smallest number that the plural word 'days' can mean is two. So two days of bleeding are also covered.

keyTerms.meaning: 'days of' – plural, so at least two

phrases.english: The verse states: 'Days';
phrases.notes: It's the same פסוק, ויקרא 15:25: 'כל ימי זוב טמאתה'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.

steps.title: What about bleeding for only one day?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know that even one day of bleeding counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know about one day?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes down one more step and asks about a single day of bleeding. This sets up the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Days' covered two days, but a plural word cannot mean one day. So one day needs a separate source.

keyTerms.meaning: one day

phrases.english: From where do we know one day?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes the question from two days down to one day.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A source that even one day of bleeding makes her טמאה.

steps.title: 'All the days' includes even one day
steps.stepSummary: The extra word 'כל' (all) includes even a single day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'All the days.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers that the word 'כל' (all) adds even one day of bleeding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ימי' alone only reaches two days. The extra word 'כל' widens the rule, so that any day of bleeding in the זיבה window counts, even just one.

keyTerms.meaning: 'all the days' – the word 'all' widens the rule to include even one day

steps.whatToRemember: Bleeding for three days, two days, or even one day during the זיבה days makes her טמאה: three days from the earlier lesson, two from 'ימי', and one from 'כל ימי'.

phrases.english: The verse states: 'All the days.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'כל' includes even a single day.

steps.title: 'Impure' teaches that a זבה makes the man טמא like a נדה
steps.stepSummary: From the word 'טמאה', a זבה makes the man who has relations with her טמא, just as a נדה does.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'She is impure' teaches that she makes the man who has relations with her טמא, like a נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא learns a new law from the word 'טמאה' in the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק compares the זבה to a נדה ('like the days of her נדה'). The word 'טמאה' teaches that this comparison covers her effect on the man too: he becomes טמא just as he would with a נדה.

keyTerms.meaning: impure
the man who has relations with her
like a נדה

phrases.english: 'Impure' —
phrases.notes: From the end of ויקרא 15:25, 'טמאה הוא'.

phrases.english: teaches that she renders the one who has relations with her impure, like a menstruating woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from which days count to the effect of her טומאה on others.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A זבה makes the man who has relations with her טמא, like a נדה does.

steps.title: 'She' – only a זבה, not a זב
steps.stepSummary: The word 'היא' limits the rule: a זבה makes the man טמא, but a זב does not make the woman he has relations with טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'She' – she makes the man who has relations with her טמא, but a זב does not make the one he has relations with טמא.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא uses the word 'היא' (she) to limit the law of the previous step to a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'she' tells us that this law applies to the זבה only. It is not turned around: a זב does not, through this law, make the woman he has relations with טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'she' – a word that limits the law to her alone
a man with an unusual discharge that makes him טמא

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume the law works in both directions. The word 'היא' teaches that it is one-way: a זבה makes the man טמא, but a זב does not have the same effect on the woman.
steps.whatToRemember: 'טמאה' teaches that a זבה makes the man who has relations with her טמא, like a נדה. 'היא' teaches that this is only for her, not for a זב.

phrases.english: 'She' —
she renders the one who has relations with her impure,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין הַזָּב מְטַמֵּא מָה שֶׁהוּא בּוֹעֵל.
phrases.english: but a זב does not render impure the one he has relations with.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the law of step 16 so that it covers only a זבה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a זבה makes the one who has relations with her טמא through this law; a זב does not.

steps.title: A logical argument that a זב should make the woman he is with טמא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests a קל וחומר: if a זבה, who is weaker in one way, makes her partner טמא, then surely a זב, who is stronger in that way, should make his partner טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't this a logical argument? A זבה does not become טמא from three sightings the way she does from three days, and still she makes the man who is with her טמא. A זב does become טמא from three sightings just as from three days. So isn't it logical that he makes the woman he is with טמא?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes back against the limit it just learned from 'היא' (step 17). It offers a קל וחומר that seems to prove a זב should make the woman he is with טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a זבה, only bleeding on separate days counts. Three sightings on one day are not like three days. For a זב, three sightings even on one day count like three days, so his טומאה is easier to trigger. The argument says: if the 'weaker' זבה passes טומאה to her partner, the 'stronger' זב certainly should.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it logical? This opens a קל וחומר argument.
A logical argument from a weaker case to a stronger one
Sightings, meaning discharges seen
The one who has relations

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think this is the final הלכה. The ברייתא raises this argument only so it can reject it with the word 'היא' in the next step.

phrases.english: But is it not a logical argument?
Just as she, who does not become impure
through sightings as through days,
phrases.notes: For a זבה, three sightings on one day do not count like bleeding on three separate days.

phrases.english: still makes the man who is with her impure,
he, who becomes impure through sightings as through days,

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ דִּין שֶׁמְּטַמֵּא מַה שֶּׁהוּא בּוֹעֵל!
phrases.english: is it not logical that he makes the one he is with impure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the limit drawn from 'היא' in step 17 with a קל וחומר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that a זב does not make the woman he is with טמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A זב's טומאה is easier to trigger than a זבה's, so he should at least match her power to make a partner טמא.

steps.title: The word 'היא' blocks the logical argument
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'היא', meaning only she makes her partner טמא. A זב does not make the woman he is with טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'she'. She makes the man who is with her impure, but a זב does not make the one he is with impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the קל וחומר by pointing to the word 'היא' in the פסוק. That word limits the rule to the זבה alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Logic alone would have extended the rule to a זב. The פסוק's word 'היא' shows the תורה meant to limit it, and a clear פסוק beats a קל וחומר. So step 17's limit holds.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches us
A man with an unusual discharge that makes him טמא

steps.whatToRemember: A זבה makes her partner טמא. A זב does not, even though a קל וחומר seemed to say he should. The word 'היא' limits the rule.

phrases.english: The verse states: 'she'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:25, 'טמאה הוא'. It's written הוא but read היא.

phrases.english: she makes the man who is with her impure,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין הַזָּב מְטַמֵּא מַה שֶּׁהוּא בּוֹעֵל.
phrases.english: but a זב does not make the one he is with impure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of step 18 by pointing to a limiting word in the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A limiting word in the פסוק overrides the logical argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A זב makes the woman he is with טמא, based on the קל וחומר
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a זבה makes her partner טמא. A זב does not.

steps.title: Source that a זבה makes beds and seats טמא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks where we learn that a זבה makes the things she lies or sits on טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that she makes a bed and a seat impure?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to a new law about a זבה and asks for its source in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משכב ומושב means things made for lying or sitting. If a זבה lies or sits on them, they become a source of טומאה. The ברייתא wants to find this in the words of the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Something made for lying or sitting, which becomes טמא when a זבה lies or sits on it
And from where do we know?

phrases.english: And from where do we know that she makes a bed and a seat impure?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new law in the ברייתא after finishing the topic of the בועל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches a זבה makes משכב ומושב טמא

steps.title: Learned from 'like the bed of her נדה time'
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק compares the זבה's bed to her bed as a נדה. So just as a נדה makes משכב ומושב טמא, a זבה does too.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'like the bed of her menstruation.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers step 20 by quoting the words 'כמשכב נדתה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows a נדה makes beds and seats טמא. The פסוק compares the זבה's bed to the נדה's bed, so the same law passes over to the זבה.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the bed of her נדה time

phrases.english: The verse states: 'like the bed of her menstruation.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The comparison 'כמשכב נדתה' gives the זבה the נדה's law of משכב ומושב.

steps.title: What about two days of bleeding?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק seems to speak about three days, which makes a full זבה. The ברייתא asks how we know the law applies after only two days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I only know this for three days. From where do we know it for two days?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks whether משכב ומושב is also טמא when she bled for only two days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three days of bleeding makes a זבה גדולה. Two days makes only a זבה קטנה. The ברייתא wants a source that the law of משכב ומושב covers the smaller case too. The same pattern of words appeared in steps 13-15, and here it is used again for משכב ומושב.

keyTerms.meaning: I only know this case
A woman who bled three days in a row
A woman who bled one or two days in a row

phrases.english: And I have only three days;
from where do we know two days?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how far the law of step 21 reaches.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a זבה after two days of bleeding makes משכב ומושב טמא

steps.title: 'Days' covers two days
steps.stepSummary: The word 'ימי', which is plural, includes two days.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'days'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers step 22: the plural word 'ימי' is enough to cover two days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The smallest plural is two. So 'days' brings in a woman who bled for two days.

keyTerms.meaning: Days of (plural)

phrases.english: The verse states 'days';

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22.

steps.title: What about one day of bleeding?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know the law applies even after a single day of bleeding.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know one day?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא pushes further and asks about the smallest case, just one day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Days' covered two days, but a plural can't mean one. So we need another word in the פסוק for a single day.

keyTerms.meaning: One day

phrases.english: From where do we know one day?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes one step lower than step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether one day of bleeding is enough for משכב ומושב to be טמא

steps.title: 'All the days' includes even one day
steps.stepSummary: The extra word 'כל' widens the law to include even one day of bleeding.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'all the days'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers step 24 with the word 'כל', meaning 'all'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'ימי' already gave us two days, so 'כל' must add something more. It adds the case of one day. Now a זבה makes משכב ומושב טמא after one, two, or three days.

keyTerms.meaning: All the days of

steps.whatToRemember: A זבה makes משכב ומושב טמא like a נדה, whether she bled one, two, or three days.

phrases.english: The verse states: 'all the days.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 24 and closes the topic of משכב ומושב.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra word 'כל' includes one day.

steps.title: Source that she counts one clean day for one day of bleeding
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how we know that a woman who bled one day counts one clean day afterward.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that she counts one day for one day?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא opens a new topic: how many clean days a זבה קטנה must count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman who sees blood on one day outside her נדה time must wait one clean day to become טהור. The ברייתא looks for this law in the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: She counts clean days
One clean day for one day of bleeding

phrases.english: And from where do we know that she counts one for one?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new law about counting clean days.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that one day of bleeding needs one clean day

steps.title: Learned from 'shall be for her'
steps.stepSummary: The words 'יהיה לה' teach that she counts one day for one day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'shall be for her.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers step 26 by quoting 'יהיה לה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads 'יהיה לה' as linking her day of bleeding to a day she must count. Each day of seeing is matched by a day of counting.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall be for her

phrases.english: The verse states: 'shall be for her.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'יהיה לה' teaches that she counts one day for one day.

steps.title: A logical argument that two days of bleeding should need seven clean days
steps.stepSummary: A קל וחומר from a זב: he does not count one for one, yet after two sightings he counts seven. So she, who does count one for one, should surely count seven after two days.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think she must count seven for two days, and it is logical. A זב does not count one for one, yet he counts seven for two. She does count one for one, so isn't it logical that she should count seven for two?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא suggests that a woman who bled two days should need seven clean days. It backs this up with a קל וחומר from the laws of a זב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב who sees once needs no clean day count, which makes his law look 'lighter'. Yet after two sightings he counts seven. A זבה who bled one day already counts a day, which makes her law look 'stricter'. So the argument says that after two days she should surely count seven.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought
Seven clean days for two sightings or days
And it is logical. This introduces a קל וחומר.

steps.confusionAlert: This קל וחומר is rejected in the next step. In fact, a זבה who bled two days counts only one clean day.

phrases.english: One might think she must count seven for two?
And it is logical:

phrases.aramaic: וּמָה הוּא, שֶׁאֵין סוֹפֵר אֶחָד לְאֶחָד,
phrases.english: Just as he, who does not count one for one,
counts seven for two,
phrases.notes: A זב who sees twice counts seven clean days.

phrases.english: she, who counts one for one,
is it not logical that she should count seven for two?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל תִּסְפּוֹר שִׁבְעָה לִשְׁנַיִם? וְדִין הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses a קל וחומר to suggest a stricter count than step 27 seemed to teach.
steps.kashyaTarget: The count for a זבה who bled two days
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the 'lighter' זב counts seven after two sightings, the 'stricter' זבה should too.

steps.title: 'Shall be for her' means she counts only her one day
steps.stepSummary: The words 'יהיה לה' limit her count: she counts only one day, even after two days of bleeding.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'shall be for her'. She counts only her day.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the קל וחומר of step 28 by reading 'יהיה לה' as a limit on how much she counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same words that taught 'one for one' also set a limit: her count stays a day, not seven. So even after two days of bleeding she counts only one clean day. Seven clean days are needed only after three days, when she is a זבה גדולה.

keyTerms.meaning: Her day, meaning a single clean day

steps.whatToRemember: A זבה קטנה, who bled one or two days, counts only one clean day. The קל וחומר from a זב is blocked by 'יהיה לה'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the הלכה of שומרת יום כנגד יום, that a woman who sees in her זיבה days waits one clean day.

phrases.english: The verse states: 'shall be for her'
she counts only her day.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״יִהְיֶה לָהּ״ — אֵינָהּ סוֹפֶרֶת אֶלָּא יוֹמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר of step 28 using the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A פסוק limits the law and overrides the logical argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: After two days of bleeding she counts seven clean days, like a זב
steps.terutzMaskana: She counts only one day, even after two days of bleeding.

steps.title: So these laws come from verses after all
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא learned the זבה laws from פסוקים, which seems to clash with calling them a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: It seems these laws come from verses!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a problem: the ברייתא we just learned gets all these זבה rules from words in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the eleven days of זיבה were called a הלכה למשה מסיני, a law passed down orally. But the ברייתא pulls every detail out of the פסוקים, so the two sources seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: It turns out / evidently
Verses (from the תורה)
A law given orally to משה at סיני, not written in a פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about what the law is. Everyone agrees on the rules; the question is only where they come from.

phrases.english: It turns out they are from verses!
phrases.notes: "They" are the laws of the eleven days of זיבה, which were called a הלכה למשה מסיני earlier.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks back at the whole ברייתא (Steps 1-29), especially its derivation of the eleven days of זיבה from פסוקים (Steps 1-11), and sets it against the earlier claim of a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier statement that the eleven days of זיבה are a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the ברייתא derives every detail from פסוקים, these laws cannot also be an oral הלכה.

steps.title: It depends on which תנא
steps.stepSummary: For רבי עקיבא the laws come from פסוקים; for רבי אלעזר בן עזריה they are a הלכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to רבי עקיבא, they come from verses. According to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, they are a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is no contradiction, because two different תנאים hold two different views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא that learns everything from פסוקים follows רבי עקיבא. The statement calling it a הלכה למשה מסיני follows רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. So each source matches a different opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: A הלכה, here meaning a law passed down orally from סיני

steps.whatToRemember: The eleven days of זיבה: for רבי עקיבא they come from פסוקים; for רבי אלעזר בן עזריה they are a הלכה למשה מסיני.

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Akiva, they are from verses;
according to Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya, they are a halakha.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא — קְרָאֵי, לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה — הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in Step 30.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the sources between two תנאים (תנאי היא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One single view holds both that the laws come from פסוקים and that they are a הלכה, which is a contradiction.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא, who learns from פסוקים; the הלכה view belongs to רבי אלעזר בן עזריה.

steps.title: Maybe daytime bleeding makes a זבה and night bleeding a נדה
steps.stepSummary: רב שמעיה suggests that since the פסוק says "days," only daytime bleeding makes her a זבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמעיה said to רבי אבא: Say that if she bleeds by day she is a זבה, but if she bleeds at night she is a נדה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שמעיה raises a challenge about how to read the פסוק of זבה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק talks about bleeding for "days." So maybe only bleeding in the daytime makes her a זבה, while bleeding at night would put her in the category of a נדה instead.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who bleeds during the days outside her regular period
A woman in her menstrual state
In the daytime
At night

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שְׁמַעְיָה לְרַבִּי אַבָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Shemaya said to Rabbi Abba:
Say that in the daytime she becomes a zava,
phrases.notes: He is reading the word "days" (ימים) in the פסוק very literally: daytime only.

phrases.english: but at night she becomes a niddah!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא, בִּימָמָא תִּהְוֵי זָבָה, בְּלֵילְיָא תִּהְוֵי נִדָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about reading the זבה פסוק, after the previous discussion was settled.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that bleeding at any time during the days of זיבה makes her a זבה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word "days" in the פסוק could mean daytime only, which would leave night bleeding as נדה.

steps.title: "Next to her נדה" means night counts too
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא shows from "על נדתה" that bleeding at night also makes her a זבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: About your question, the פסוק says "beyond her נדה," meaning right next to her נדה. When is right next to her נדה? At night, and the פסוק calls her a זבה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא answers רב שמעיה with a proof from the words of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words "על נדתה" teach that bleeding right after her נדה days makes her a זבה. The first time right after those days is a night, since a Jewish day starts at night. Since the פסוק calls night bleeding at that time זבה, night bleeding cannot be a separate נדה category.

keyTerms.meaning: "Beyond her נדה," the words in the פסוק
Right next to (right after) her days of נדה
About your point, the פסוק says

steps.whatToRemember: Bleeding at night during the days of זיבה also makes a woman a זבה, as learned from "על נדתה."

phrases.english: He said to him: About you, the verse says:
"Beyond her niddah" means close to her niddah.
When is the time close to her niddah?
At night, and the verse calls her a zava.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב שמעיה's challenge from Step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Proof from another word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "Days" means daytime only, so night bleeding would make her a נדה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The time right after her נדה days is a night, and the פסוק still calls her a זבה, so night bleeding counts as זיבה.

steps.title: Learning הלכות every day brings עולם הבא
steps.stepSummary: דבי אליהו teaches that whoever learns הלכות daily is promised עולם הבא, based on reading הליכות as הלכות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in דבי אליהו: Whoever learns הלכות every day is promised a place in עולם הבא, as it says "הליכות עולם לו." Do not read it "הליכות" (ways) but "הלכות" (laws).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes the whole מסכת with a statement about the reward for learning הלכות every day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says "הליכות עולם לו," "the ways of the world are his." By reading הליכות as הלכות, the teaching becomes: someone who has הלכות has the eternal world, meaning עולם הבא.

keyTerms.meaning: One who learns/reviews הלכות
He is promised
Someone who has a share in עולם הבא
Do not read it as... (a way to learn an extra lesson from a word)

steps.whatToRemember: Whoever learns הלכות every day is promised עולם הבא.
steps.confusionAlert: "אל תקרי" does not change the פסוק. It keeps the written words and draws an extra lesson by reading a word in a different way.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the famous closing line of מסכת נדה, encouraging daily learning of הלכות.

phrases.english: It was taught in the school of Eliyahu:
Anyone who learns halakhot every day

phrases.aramaic: מוּבְטָח לוֹ שֶׁהוּא בֶּן הָעוֹלָם הַבָּא,
phrases.english: is promised that he has a share in the World to Come,
as it says: "The ways of the world are his."
Do not read "ways" but rather "halakhot."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new closing teaching, not connected to the זבה discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Learning הלכות every day guarantees a share in עולם הבא.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק תינוקת and מסכת נדה
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula for פרק תינוקת and for all of מסכת נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק תינוקת, and מסכת נדה is complete.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the formal closing line marking the end of the פרק and of the whole מסכת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is said at the end of every פרק as a promise to come back and learn it again. Here it also announces that the whole of מסכת נדה is finished.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you
And it is completed
Tractate

steps.whatToRemember: מסכת נדה ends with פרק תינוקת and the promise of עולם הבא for daily learning of הלכות.

phrases.english: We will return to you, Tinoket,
phrases.notes: תינוקת is the name of this פרק, taken from its first word.

phrases.english: and Tractate Niddah is completed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the פרק and the מסכת after the final teaching.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פרק תינוקת and all of מסכת נדה are complete.
